title: The Salt Rivergate
premise: Wendell Ishikawa has spent seven years flying medicine and mail into the interior, hiding from the wreckage of the Salt Rivergate expedition that made his name and killed his best friend. When his old rival Marguerite Voss buys out his debt and forces him to fly her crew to the forbidden headwaters before the snows close the range, he discovers she's chasing the same salvage he swore off—and that someone in her crew is sabotaging them for a buyer who wants the rivergate's secrets buried forever. Betrayed at the last passable airstrip, Wendell must lead the survivors overland through the monsoon to reach the gate first, where he finally confronts what really happened the night his friend died. He chooses to destroy the salvage rather than let it be owned, trading his invisibility for a place among the people of the interior who never stopped counting him as one of their own.
about_author: Rafael Lockridge is a former bush pilot turned novelist who spent a decade flying cargo across remote mountain ranges before an injury grounded him for good. He writes adventure fiction from a cabin near the confluence of two unnamed rivers, where he insists the mail plane still comes every Thursday.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Cargo
chapters.summary: Wendell ferries vaccines and gossip to river villages, establishing his careful routines and the debt shadowing his aircraft. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of a man who has made smallness his armor.

chapters.title: Marguerite at the Fence
chapters.summary: Marguerite Voss arrives unannounced with paperwork owning Wendell's debt and an offer he can't refuse: one flight to the headwaters. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: dread dressed as opportunity; the past landing on his airstrip like weather.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: Voss introduces her team—surveyor Okafor, mechanic Delia, quiet fixer Bram—each carrying reasons of their own. Wendell reads them like instruments. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: wary calculation; trust as a currency he no longer holds.

chapters.title: Fuel, Lies, and Weather
chapters.summary: Preparations reveal the job's true destination: the Salt Rivergate, site of the disaster. Wendell nearly walks away until Voss reveals she knows how his friend Elio died. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: rage and grief colliding into reluctant consent.

chapters.title: Last Town Before the Range
chapters.summary: The crew stages at a frontier town where old-timers recognize Wendell and won't say why they look at him that way. A stranger photographs their aircraft. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the unease of being recognized by a past he fled.

chapters.title: Into the Throat
chapters.summary: First mountain leg through worsening weather; Wendell's skill dazzles the crew but the route forces him near the crash corridor he's avoided for years. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: muscle memory of fear, and the strange comfort of competence.

chapters.title: Okafor's Maps
chapters.summary: Surveyor Okafor shows Wendell maps predating the official record, proving Voss knew the gate's location all along. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: a professional's conscience beginning to itch.

chapters.title: The Village That Counts Planes
chapters.summary: A forced fuel stop at a village where children greet Wendell by name—he's been delivering medicine here for years without knowing he was expected. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: belonging witnessed from outside; Delia sees what Wendell cannot.

chapters.title: Bram in the Night
chapters.summary: Delia catches Bram tampering with the radio. He claims maintenance; she doesn't believe him but says nothing yet. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: suspicion tightening like a tourniquet.

chapters.title: Storm Gate
chapters.summary: A storm pins the crew at a high meadow strip. Around the fire, Voss tells her version of the Salt Rivergate expedition—and it contradicts everything Wendell remembers. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: vertigo of unreliable memory.

chapters.title: Elio's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the original expedition, Elio's charisma, the discovery they swore to bury, and the night everything burned. POV: Wendell (past). Emotional beat: love and guilt braided together; the wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: News arrives by radio: the monsoon is early. The window over the range narrows from days to hours. Voss pushes harder; Wendell calculates survival odds and hates the answer. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: time becoming an antagonist.

chapters.title: Delia Confides
chapters.summary: Delia tells Wendell about Bram and the radio. Together they find a second transmitter hidden in cargo crates—someone is reporting their position. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: alliance forming in the dark; fear shared is fear halved.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Shadow
chapters.summary: A chartered plane shadows them. Bram admits under pressure he was hired to track, not sabotage—but by whom, even he isn't sure anymore. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: a mercenary discovering his leash has a hand on the other end.

chapters.title: Whiteout Crossing
chapters.summary: They attempt the high pass early to beat both storm and shadow. Ice on the wings, a near-fatal downdraft, Wendell threading a canyon by memory. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into grace—the finest flying of his life.

chapters.title: Down at Drowned Meadow
chapters.summary: A rough landing bends the gear. Stranded above the treeline with the monsoon arriving, the crew must go overland. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: helplessness giving way to resolve; the sky taken from them.

chapters.title: What Voss Carries
chapters.summary: Okafor confronts Voss privately: she carries Elio's old field journal, which she claims he gave her willingly. Wendell finds out. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: betrayal layered on betrayal; loyalty fracturing along old seams.

chapters.title: The Long Traverse
chapters.summary: Days of overland travel through rain-soaked passes. Rations shrink, tempers fray, and Wendell proves he knows this country better than any map. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: grudging respect hardening into something like fellowship.

chapters.title: River Country
chapters.summary: They descend into the watershed where villagers shelter the crew. An elder tells Wendell that Elio spent his final week here—and left something behind. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: grief finding a door it never had before.

chapters.title: Elio's Letter
chapters.summary: The elder gives Wendell a letter Elio wrote the night before he died. It names the buyer's organization and warns that the gate must stay closed. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the dead speaking plainly at last; sorrow turning to purpose.

chapters.title: Voss Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted with the letter, Voss confesses: she wasn't hired to recover the salvage—she was hired to confirm it still exists, and her employer will level the valley if she fails. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: a proud woman's armor cracking; fear masquerading as ambition.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Bram's real handler contacts him via the hidden transmitter: bring the journal or the charter plane arrives with men who won't negotiate. Bram hesitates for the first time in his career. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: a mercenary feeling the pull of people who fed him when he was starving.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: The advance team reaches them first. A violent standoff at a river crossing; Okafor takes a bullet shielding the journal. They drive the attackers off but lose their radio and two days. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: blood price paid; the adventure becomes a fight for survival.

chapters.title: Fever Watch
chapters.summary: Okafor's wound turns septic. Villagers bring medicine Wendell once delivered; now the debt runs the other way. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: reciprocity revealed—the years of small kindnesses were not invisible after all.

chapters.title: The Gate Road
chapters.summary: Guided by the elder's grandson, they follow an overgrown trail toward the headwaters. The terrain grows stranger: terraces, carved stones, evidence the gate was built, not found. POV: Okafor (feverish, drifting). Emotional beat: awe undercut by mortality; wonder through delirium.

chapters.title: Charter on the Ridge
chapters.summary: The buyer's plane lands armed men on the ridge above them. The crew splits: Delia leads a decoy party while Wendell and Voss push for the gate. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: courage chosen freely by people with every excuse not to.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell and Voss reach the Salt Rivergate: a vast engineered sluice system, ancient and deliberate, that the old expedition meant to sell piece by piece. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: understanding replacing mystery—the gate controls water for everyone downstream, or enriches whoever owns it.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The buyer himself arrives by helicopter—civilized, reasonable, offering Wendell everything: debt cleared, name restored, Elio's death reframed as heroism. All he must do is walk away. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: temptation as a mirror; corruption offered politely.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss realizes her employer intends to leave no witnesses to the valley's existence. She turns her evidence against him, buying Wendell time at gunpoint. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: redemption seized late and at cost; power refusing its own corruption.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Wendell and Bram, unlikely partners, rig the gate's mechanisms to fail catastrophically for anyone attempting removal—while preserving its function for the valley. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: a fixer fixing something that matters; skill redeemed.

chapters.title: The Flood Season Argument
chapters.summary: The buyer's men breach the upper sluice to force compliance, threatening downstream villages. Wendell must choose: save the gate intact or flood it deliberately to save the villages. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—power over water versus water for the people.

chapters.title: Breaking the Gate
chapters.summary: Wendell triggers the controlled collapse he and Bram designed. The gate dies as salvage and lives as ruin, its waters running free. The buyer's operation drowns in paperwork and mud. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: destruction as fidelity; keeping a promise seven years late.

chapters.title: Helicopter Down
chapters.summary: The buyer attempts escape; Voss grounds the helicopter with a well-placed charge and stands waiting when he climbs out. The advance team surrenders to arriving rangers tipped off by Delia's decoy radio work. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: justice delivered without ceremony; the powerful meeting consequences.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Valley
chapters.summary: Rangers, villagers, and battered crew take stock. Okafor survives. The buyer faces charges built on Voss's records and Okafor's maps. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: exhaustion edged with peace; the ledger balanced.

chapters.title: Debt Forgiven
chapters.summary: With the buyer arrested, Voss tears up the papers owning Wendell's debt—and offers him partnership instead. He declines the partnership but accepts the forgiveness. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: freedom arriving quietly, without fanfare.

chapters.title: The Question of Going Home
chapters.summary: Voss offers Wendell a legitimate survey contract; Delia asks him to come south; the village offers him land. Every door open, Wendell realizes he already is home. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than defaulted.

chapters.title: Flying the Wreck Corridor
chapters.summary: Wendell flies the route he avoided for seven years and scatters Elio's letter's ashes-page over the crash site, reading the rest aloud at the village. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: mourning completed; the ghost given rest.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Snow closes the range behind them. The crew winters over in the valley—stories, repairs, Delia teaching children engines, Bram deciding to stay. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: warmth earned; a found family settling in.

chapters.title: Spring Runoff
chapters.summary: Months later, Wendell flies the first post-thaw mail run, the free-running river glittering below. Voss's letters arrive with contracts he actually wants. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: renewal; the world opening like a thawed river.

chapters.title: The Salt Rivergate
chapters.summary: Final chapter mirrors the first: a routine flight, small cargo, familiar voices on the radio—but now Wendell flies as a man known, owed nothing, belonging everywhere along the river. He banks toward home as the title place gleams in ruins that hold. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: arrival; identity no longer hidden but lived.
